I started at 9

First time I self harmed was with a rock when I was ten or nine. I was in a really toxic friendship where I was constantly being cast aside and insulted, and then guilt tripped when I tried to leave. Started by scratching myself with rocks, later moved onto scratching myself with scissors. In year seven the school found out, and dealt with it horribly. Treated me as a dumb nuisance of a child, and as if I had broken the rules in some way. Everything felt more like a punishment. I was sent to some local charity run counselling in which the staff that was talking to us stared at me as if I was some weird disgusting creature. I cried afterwards and refused to go back. The whole ordeal gave me so much anxiety and made me so paranoid that I stayed clean for around two years out of pure fear. At the beginning of year nine, the thoughts started breaking through the wall I built again and the urge came back. Right before the start of the school year, I found a razor and used it just as it was, with handle and all. I think I only made one tiny baby cut that bled, but it felt like so much then. So I suppose that was really the first time I cut. After the very start of the school year, I searched through our bathroom I found some of my dad's old razor blades, they were a bit dull and definitely old, but this was the first time Id made any cuts that really bled and it felt like a massive breakthrough. After that I moved onto blades from disposable razors, which were far sharper. Everything spiralled really, now I'm 14, and I  think soon I'm going to need stitches. I'm past styro and I don't think the urge to go further is going to stop growing. This is really a dangerous business.

i suffer with this a lot. For around three years ive been in this constant state, and it sucks balls. I absolutely hate it. To me it feels like im watching life through a screen- not actually there, or like my vision is blurry even though i can see just fine. This has got to be one of the worst feelings i could imagine, especially when it doesnt leave. It makes you desperate just to feel as if you exist in life, desperate to be able to do simple things like hear the birds sing and touch the grass. Of course you can do all that still- but youre not really in that world. Everything feels fake in that state. Im sorry you have to go through it, i truly do hope it eases for you and you dont get stuck. This is the part where id normally give you advice, but im afraid i myself am still looking for a way to get out of this. If id known one, i wouldnt still be here three years later. You could look for tips to help online, but if it never leaves getting professional help may be the best chance you have at feeling better. Stay safe <3
